subject: Post-demo: Observability comparison & prioritized validation checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Summers <claire@nebulaai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Observability comparison & prioritized validation checklist

Hi Claire / Sanjay —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Quick recap and a suggested set of prioritized validation steps so your infra team can compare Redwood vs your hyperscaler-managed endpoints and other inference APIs. I attached a compact checklist (redwood-observability-checklist.xlsx) and uploaded the demo recording.

High-level takeaways from our call:
- Nebula cares most about per-request telemetry (per-token and end-to-end), cost attribution by route, and integrated tracing into existing APMs.
- Hyperscaler solutions gave basic token counts and VM-level metrics but lacked: fine-grained per-route dashboards, automatic KV cache visibility, and built-in per-token latency breakdowns (decode/encode/kvs).
- For initial validation we recommend a 72-hour synthetic run + two focused tests: trace correlation across client -> edge -> model runtime, and per-token breakdown under variable sequence lengths.

Prioritized validation checklist (high level) — see attachment for details:
1) Trace correlation (critical): send 500 synthetic requests / minute for 30 minutes, verify trace IDs propagate from app to model runtime and appear in Datadog/NewRelic.
2) Per-token latency breakdown: run variable-length prompts (32/256/1024) and compare p50/p95 for each decode step.
3) KV cache visibility: exercise repeated prefix pattern, confirm hit/miss metrics and cache-stats export.
4) Cost attribution by route: generate mixed workload (chat + embeddings + rerank) and ensure token-level metering maps to HubSpot billing reports.
5) Log export formats: validate JSONL export compatibility and ingestion into existing log pipeline.

Asks / next steps:
- Claire/Sanjay: please confirm which hyperscaler endpoints + model variants you want us to match in the checklist (we'll fill in config knobs).
- Ben/Marissa/Vanessa: can you own the internal test runs? I propose Ben lead trace correlation, Marissa owns per-token profiling, and Vanessa validates dashboard exports.

I'll schedule a short sync early next week to align on exact test harness and share a preconfigured k6 script and Datadog dashboard JSON.

Cheers,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Summers <claire@nebulaai.com>

Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Observability comparison & prioritized validation checklist

Jordan —

Really useful summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side before we run anything:

- Hyperscaler targets: please include AWS Bedrock endpoint (bedrock-prod.nebula) and our GCP-managed vertex endpoint (vertex-nb1). We also want to compare against the vendor API we currently use for embeddings (embedly.ai).
- For trace correlation: we require trace IDs to be visible in both our APM and in the model runtime logs (not just request ids).
- For per-token metrics: sample at three sequence lengths (32/512/2048) and include p50/p95/p99.

Sanjay will be our technical owner and will coordinate infra to run synthetic traffic. He can take the checklist and run the tests if we provide the harness.

One ask from procurement: can you include a short statement about what telemetry we can store in our KMS-backed logs vs what is masked by default? We need that for our security team.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Summers | Head of Platform
Nebula AI
claire@nebulaai.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Observability comparison & prioritized validation checklist

Thanks Claire — good call. Short responses and actions below.

- Targets: we'll add AWS Bedrock (bedrock-prod.nebula), GCP Vertex (vertex-nb1), and embedly.ai to the checklist matrix.
- Trace IDs: Redwood runtime supports full trace propagation (we instrument and emit OpenTelemetry compatible span IDs). We'll provide a small example showing a trace ID appearing in a Datadog span and in the runtime log line.
- Per-token sampling: we'll include 32/512/2048 as requested and capture p50/p95/p99.
- Telemetry / masking note: we will deliver a one-paragraph KMS masking statement for your security team (what is masked by default, and what can be exported under an approved key).

Internal owners (confirming):
- Ben Carter: lead trace correlation test + Datadog dashboard JSON (target: 4/21 run)
- Marissa Cole: per-token profiling scripts + profiling dashboard (target: 4/22 run)
- Vanessa Ortiz: log export & JSONL compatibility, HubSpot cost mapping (target: 4/22 run)

Claire/Sanjay — I'll put together the preconfigured k6 scenario, a Datadog dashboard JSON, and a short telemetry masking statement by Monday EOD (4/20). If that works, can Sanjay confirm a 90-minute window on 4/21 for the initial trace correlation run?

On attachments: I updated the checklist spreadsheet with the hyperscaler columns and the test parameters.

Best,
Jordan
